correctness.rationale: The stable saddle determinant and eigenvector direction are exact. In the backward-invariant strip 0<x<r, mu>r^2, the stable branch is global and meets each higher section once. The exact dmu/dx formula yields 0<=mu_epsilon(eta)-r^2<=epsilon*a/r*log(r/eta) at every fixed eta. The exact dlog(x)/dmu relation and uniform denominator control then prove the action with epsilon first and eta second, including strict positivity and relative action. The numerical package checks finite examples only; no extrapolation from samples is used.

originality.rationale: The January 2026 original introduces the exact adaptive-pitchfork system, documents its globally extending singular funnel and exponential narrowing, and identifies the stable basin boundary. Its complete main text and supplementary section II do not state the fixed-section epsilon-to-zero action A(mu)=mu-r^2-b log((mu+b)/(r^2+b)), nor the cancellation of the feedback parameter from the rate between sections. General entry-exit results cover related slow-fast effects but treat other dimensional or spectral arrangements; they provide relevant methods, not this stated model-specific formula. The claim refines a known phenomenon rather than rediscovering it. Priority is provisional, notably because general asymptotic theorems could imply a specialization.
residual_risks: More general geometric singular perturbation or entry–exit results might imply the model-specific coefficient as an immediate specialization.

value.rationale: This is a natural quantitative stability invariant of a genuine two-attractor slow-fast system: the horizontal coordinate of its saddle basin separator on a fixed slow-parameter section. The exact exponential cost determines the sharp basin-threshold sensitivity, not just the existence of a thin funnel. The cancellation of the feedback coefficient between sections separates universal drift-controlled attenuation from the parameter-dependent saddle anchor. These are meaningful geometric facts motivated by the source phenomenon, not a free parameter substitution.
